acceptOwnership().details: The new owner accepts the ownership transfer.

canReturnTransferRestrictionCode(uint8).details: Returns true if the restriction code exists, and false otherwise. Rule authors should use unique restriction codes across rules when possible. If a code is intentionally shared by multiple rules, all of them should return the same message for that code in `messageForTransferRestriction`.

returns._0: True if the restriction code is known by this rule, false otherwise.

returns.isValid: => true if the transfer is valid, false otherwise

canTransfer(address,address,uint256,uint.details: This function must not modify state.  It may enforce checks such as:   - Allowlist / blocklist membership   - Freezing rules   - Transfer limitations   - Jurisdictional, regulatory, or policy-driven restrictions  If the transfer is not allowed, this function MUST return `false`.

params.amount: The amount being transferred (always `1` for ERC-721).
params.from: The address currently holding the token.
params.to: The address intended to receive the token.
params.tokenId: The ERC-721/1155 token ID being transferred.

returns._0: `true` if the transfer is permitted, otherwise `false`.

canTransferFrom(address,address,address,.details: Does not check balances or access rights (Access Control).

params.value: The number of tokens to transfer.

returns._0: isCompliant True if the transfer complies with policy.

canTransferFrom(address,address,address,.details: - MUST NOT modify state.  - Implementations SHOULD use `detectTransferRestrictionFrom` internally.

returns._0: `true` if the transfer is permitted, otherwise `false`.

params.forwarderIrrevocable: Address of the ERC-2771 forwarder for meta-transactions.
params.sanctionContractOracle_: Chainalysis sanctions oracle used to screen addresses.

detectTransferRestriction(address,addres.details: See {ERC-1404} This function is where an issuer enforces the restriction logic of their token transfers.  Some examples of this might include: - checking if the token recipient is whitelisted,  - checking if a sender's tokens are frozen in a lock-up period, etc.

returns._0: uint8 restricted code, 0 means the transfer is authorized

detectTransferRestriction(address,addres.details: - MUST NOT modify state.  - MUST return `0` when the transfer is allowed.  - Non-zero codes SHOULD follow the ERC-1404 or RuleEngine restriction-code conventions.

params.amount: The amount being transferred (always `1` for ERC-721).
params.from: The address currently holding the token.
params.to: The address intended to receive the token.
params.tokenId: The ERC-721/1155 token ID being checked.

returns._0: A restriction code: `0` for success, otherwise an implementation-defined error code.

detectTransferRestrictionFrom(address,ad.details: See {ERC-1404} Add an additionnal argument `spender` This function is where an issuer enforces the restriction logic of their token transfers.  Some examples of this might include: - checking if the token recipient is whitelisted,  - checking if a sender's tokens are frozen in a lock-up period, etc.

params.spender: The address initiating the delegated transfer.

returns._0: uint8 restricted code, 0 means the transfer is authorized

detectTransferRestrictionFrom(address,ad.details: Similar to `detectTransferRestriction`, but includes the spender performing the transfer.  - MUST NOT modify state.  - MUST return `0` when transfer is allowed.

params.from: The current owner of the token.
params.spender: The caller executing the transfer (owner, operator, or approved address).
params.value: The amount being transferred (always `1` for ERC-721).

returns._0: A restriction code: `0` for allowed, otherwise a non-zero restriction identifier.

isTrustedForwarder(address).details: Indicates whether any particular address is the trusted forwarder.

messageForTransferRestriction(uint8).details: See {ERC-1404} This function is effectively an accessor for the "message", a human-readable explanation as to why a transaction is restricted.

params.restrictionCode: The restriction code to translate into a message.

owner().details: Returns the address of the current owner.

pendingOwner().details: Returns the address of the pending owner.

renounceOwnership().details: Leaves the contract without owner. It will not be possible to call `onlyOwner` functions. Can only be called by the current owner. NOTE: Renouncing ownership will leave the contract without an owner, thereby disabling any functionality that is only available to the owner.

setSanctionListOracle(address).details: Restricted to the sanction-list manager; reverts on the zero address.

params.interfaceId: The interface identifier, as specified in ERC-165.

returns._0: True if the interface is supported.

transferOwnership(address).details: Starts the ownership transfer of the contract to a new account. Replaces the pending transfer if there is one. Can only be called by the current owner. Setting `newOwner` to the zero address is allowed; this can be used to cancel an initiated ownership transfer.

params.ctx: The fungible transfer context describing the transfer.

transferred(address,address,address,uint.details: Must revert if the operation is not allowed. Same function as CMTAT's `IRuleEngine.transferred(spender, from, to, value)`, declared here so that `IRule` does not inherit the compliance reads of `IRuleEngine`. A zero `value` carries no economic meaning: a stateful rule must treat it as a no-op (see the warning in CMTAT's `IRuleEngine`).

params.from: The origin address, zero on a mint.
params.spender: The account that initiated the operation.
params.to: The destination address, zero on a burn.
